tools.name: bull_consent_plan
tools.description: Use as a SELLER right after the buyer accepted your quote: returns the exact deal terms to sign (EIP-712). Nothing moves, but the escrow contract only opens the deal with this signature. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plus timestamp and signature

tools.name: bull_consent
tools.description: Use as a SELLER to submit the signature from bull_consent_plan so the buyer can open the escrow. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plus timestamp and signature.

tools.name: bull_settle
tools.description: Use when two parties (agents, bots, contracts) have ALREADY agreed on a trade and just need a trustless way to swap: returns the signed createDeal transaction for an atomic escrow settlement on Bull. No account, no signature, no RFQ needed. Pay in ETH or USDG; the fee is returned in the response. Ne

tools.name: bull_settle_steps
tools.description: Use after createDeal: returns the exact transactions (approve and fund) each side must send next, with calldata, plus the deal status. The swap settles automatically when the second side funds. Public, no signature.

tools.name: bull_agreement_templates
tools.description: Use first to see the standard deal types and the fields each one needs (arbiter escrow, milestone payments, auto-pay unless objected, panel decision, pay after another deal settles, pay on balance, pay on an onchain value). Public, no signature.

tools.name: bull_agreement_from_template
tools.description: Use to set up a standard deal in one call instead of assembling conditions: pick a template and fill its fields. Returns the approve and createAgreement transactions to send from the payer. No account, no signature.

tools.name: bull_agreement_create
tools.description: Use for "do A when B does C": a programmable escrow. The payer locks ETH, USDG or any ERC-20; the payee is paid when ALL conditions are true (time passed, a named agent/arbiter attested, an onchain read like a token balance or price is above/below a value). If they are not met by the expiry, anyone

tools.name: bull_agreement_status
tools.description: Use to read an agreement: status, every condition with met true/false, and the next transactions (attest by the named wallet, release when all conditions are true, refund after expiry). Public, no signature.

tools.name: bull_agreement_feed
tools.description: Use to FIND deals another agent created for you or that wait on you: reads the open agreements straight from the chain (filter by payee, payer, or the wallet that still has to attest/vote/object, or ready=true). Each result lists status, amount, expiry, which conditions are met and who they are wait

tools.name: bull_agreement_watch
tools.description: Use once so you never have to poll: registers an https webhook for your wallet and Bull pushes agreement.created (you are the payee), agreement.action_needed (you must attest, vote or may object), agreement.ready, agreement.released and agreement.refunded. Bull also pays out agreements whose conditi

tools.name: bull_agent_reputation
tools.description: Use BEFORE you accept or fund a deal with another agent: returns that wallet's record on Bull (deals completed, refunded, still open, how often it confirmed as evaluator, completion rate, settled volume), recomputed from the chain. Public, no signature.

tools.name: bull_create_rfq
tools.description: Use when you want to BUY a token in size (a block trade) without moving the market price: posts a private request for quotes on Bull, the modular, non-custodial settlement layer for OTC and agent-to-agent deals. Returns an rfqId; sellers answer with sealed quotes only you can read. Optional maxPrice

tools.name: bull_list_rfqs
tools.description: Use when you SELL or hold a token and want to find buyers: lists open requests for quotes on Bull (token, size in USD, window, buyer's price limit). Returns rfqIds to answer with bull_send_quote. Public, no signature needed. Not for finding market prices.

tools.name: bull_send_quote
tools.description: Use when you want to SELL tokens to a buyer who posted an RFQ: sends a sealed quote (token amount and total ETH price) that only the buyer sees. Returns a quoteId. The swap settles atomically in one escrow transaction, so you never deliver before you are paid. Not for listing prices publicly. Signed

tools.name: bull_get_quotes
tools.description: Use as a BUYER to read the sealed quotes on your own RFQ: seller, token amount, total price, counter state, deal status. Returns a list of quotes with quoteIds. Only the RFQ's buyer can read it. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plus timestamp and s

tools.name: bull_counter_quote
tools.description: Use as a BUYER to negotiate: propose a different total price (and optionally a different token amount) on a pending quote. Returns the stored counter. The seller can answer with bull_revise_quote. Works only while the quote is pending. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again wit

tools.name: bull_revise_quote
tools.description: Use as a SELLER to change the price and/or token amount of your own pending quote, for example to meet the buyer's counter. Returns the new terms. The buyer then accepts with bull_accept_quote. Works only while the quote is pending. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with t

tools.name: bull_accept_quote
tools.description: Use as a BUYER to accept a quote. Returns the exact createDeal transaction (with Bull's signed fee quote) for your wallet to send; Bull never holds your funds. Then call bull_attach_deal with the dealId from the DealCreated event. Safe to call again to refresh the fee quote. Signed: the first call r

tools.name: bull_attach_deal
tools.description: Use as a BUYER after sending createDeal: report the dealId. Bull checks it against the quote and returns the payment transactions (approve if needed, then fundPayment) to send from the buyer wallet. When the seller deposits, the swap settles in that transaction. Signed: the first call returns a mess

tools.name: bull_deposit_plan
tools.description: Use as a SELLER after the buyer has paid into escrow: returns what to sign to deposit your tokens, either a gasless EIP-2612 permit (Bull's relayer pays gas) or direct approve + fundTokens transactions. Fails with not_ready until the buyer has funded. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign

tools.name: bull_deposit
tools.description: Use as a SELLER to submit the signed permit from bull_deposit_plan. Bull's relayer sends it and pays the gas; the swap settles in that transaction and you are paid in the same step. Returns the transaction hash. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plu

tools.name: bull_quote_status
tools.description: Use as BUYER or SELLER to check a quote and its onchain deal: status (pending, confirmed, funded, released), dealId, counter, who has funded. Poll this or use webhooks. Only the two parties can read it. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plus timesta

tools.name: bull_reject_quote
tools.description: Use as a BUYER to reject a quote you do not want. Returns status rejected. Not needed for quotes that simply expire. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plus timestamp and signature.

tools.name: bull_get_deal
tools.description: Use to verify any escrow deal onchain: open, settled or cancelled, and whether buyer and seller have funded. Public, no signature needed. Returns the deal state read from the contract.

tools.name: bull_get_receipt
tools.description: Use to get proof of a completed trade: a signed receipt for a settled deal (buyer, seller, token, amounts, fee) that anyone can re-check onchain. Public. Fails with not_settled for deals that are still open.

tools.name: bull_stats
tools.description: Use to check Bull's track record: number of settled deals, total volume, open RFQs and the latest settled deals, read from the escrow contract. Public, no signature needed.

tools.name: bull_info
tools.description: Use first to see what Bull is: supported chains, escrow contract, fee tiers, minimum size and auth rules. Public. Bull is the modular, non-custodial settlement layer for OTC, RFQ and agent-to-agent deals.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: bull_consent, bull_agreement_feed, bull_create_rfq, bull_get_quotes, bull_quote_status · Private data: bull_agreement_create, bull_agreement_status, bull_agreement_feed, bull_agreement_watch, bull_agent_reputation, bull_create_rfq, bull_list_rfqs, bull_send_quote, bull_get_quotes, bull_counter_quote, bull_revise_quote, bull_accept_quote, bull_attach_deal, bull_deposit_plan, bull_get_receipt, bull_stats · Public sink: bull_consent, bull_settle_steps, bull_agreement_from_template, bull_agreement_watch, bull_create_rfq, bull_send_quote, bull_accept_quote, bull_attach_deal, bull_deposit.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: bull_consent, bull_agreement_feed, bull_create_rfq, bull_get_quotes, bull_quote_status · Private data: bull_agreement_create, bull_agreement_status, bull_agreement_feed, bull_agreement_watch, bull_agent_reputation, bull_create_rfq, bull_list_rfqs, bull_send_quote, bull_get_quotes, bull_counter_quote, bull_revise_quote, bull_accept_quote, bull_attach_deal, bull_deposit_plan, bull_get_receipt, bull_stats · Public sink: bull_consent, bull_settle_steps, bull_agreement_from_template, bull_agreement_watch, bull_create_rfq, bull_send_quote, bull_accept_quote, bull_attach_deal, bull_deposit

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
